param.name: in_features
param.dialogReference: Features to evaluate for proximity. For REST requests, provide a feature layer URL, for example https://.../FeatureServer/0.

param.name: input_where_clause
param.dialogReference: Optional SQL expression used to filter input features before proximity analysis. Use a physical field name from the input layer schema, not a field alias, and a verified value. For example, FIELD_NAME = 'verified value' only when the field and value exist in the selected layer. Leave blank to evaluate all input features.

param.name: proximity_features
param.dialogReference: Reference features used to find nearby input features. For REST requests, provide a feature layer URL, for example https://.../FeatureServer/0.

param.name: proximity_where_clause
param.dialogReference: Optional SQL expression used to filter proximity features before analysis. Use a physical field name from the proximity layer schema, not a field alias, and a verified value. For example, FIELD_NAME = 'verified value' only when the field and value exist in the selected layer. Leave blank to use all proximity features.

param.name: search_distance
param.dialogReference: Geodesic distance used for the selection. Example: 500 Meters or 2 Miles.

param.name: out_features
param.dialogReference: New feature class containing input features within the search distance. Example: C:\data\analysis.gdb\issues_near_schools.

param.name: selected_feature_count
param.dialogReference: The number of input features within the specified distance of the filtered proximity features.

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Returns input features within a user-specified geodesic distance of user-supplied reference features.
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Use this tool when the features to evaluate and the reference features must be chosen at run time. Before supplying either optional SQL where clause, inspect the selected layer's schema and use its physical field names and verified values, not display aliases. The SQL must use the dialect accepted by the referenced feature service. For example, use FIELD_NAME = 'verified value' only when the field and value are confirmed in the selected layer. Leave a where clause blank to include all features from that layer. Use the selected_feature_count output to answer count questions.
